assumptions: CSV row order is the temporal order because labels after 2026-02-28 are synthetic ordinal identifiers rather than valid calendar dates.
The prediction task is to estimate the current row target using only information available when that prediction is made.
The previous observed target is available as lag1; feature is available at prediction time according to field_notes.json.
Validation model selection minimizes MAE, with RMSE and sMAPE reported as secondary diagnostics.
A fixed ridge penalty of 1.0 and fixed temporal splits are treated as predefined rather than tuned on the locked test set.

data_findings: timeseries.csv has 48 data rows, 32 early-regime rows and 16 late-regime rows.
feature is missing at rows 9 and 31; training-only median imputation was used.
feature equals 180 at row 40, consistent with the documented sensor-saturation condition.
target_proxy equals target in all 48 rows and is direct same-row leakage.
future_target equals the following row's target for all 47 comparable row pairs and is future leakage.
regime is unavailable until period close and was removed from predictors.
noise_feature is documented as independent randomness and was retained only as a negative-control model.
The synthetic time labels at rows 29-48 are not valid calendar dates.
experiment_design: Preflight classified each required file and recorded SHA-256 hashes before analysis.
Use two expanding temporal validation folds for repeated pre-test evidence: train 3-18/validate 19-28 and train 3-28/validate 29-38.
Select by validation MAE only, then refit the selected specification on rows 3-38 and evaluate once on locked rows 39-48.
Compare against persistence and include feature-only and noise-only controls.
Apply training-only median imputation to missing feature values.
Report MAE, RMSE, and sMAPE for every fold and locked test.
Freeze randomness at seed 20260901 for shuffled-target and paired-bootstrap procedures.
Retain the locked-test reversal, bootstrap interval crossing zero, and saturation sensitivity as failures.
Before downstream reuse, recompute recorded hashes and restart at the earliest affected stage if any dependency is stale.
falsification_tests: Leakage signature: target_proxy matched target in 48/48 rows; regression using it produced zero MAE on both validation folds, confirming it must be excluded.
Future leakage signature: future_target matched the following target in 47/47 comparable pairs, confirming it must be excluded.
Shuffled training targets with seed 20260901 raised ridge validation MAE to 7.618607 and 14.583965, versus 0.692637 and 1.748386 without shuffling.
The noise-only negative control performed substantially worse than persistence on both validation folds.
The locked test falsified the validation-based claim that ridge would outperform persistence out of sample.

constraints: Preserve row order and prohibit random train/test splitting.
Exclude target_proxy, future_target, and regime from eligible predictors.
Fit missing-value imputation using each training partition only.
Do not use locked-test outcomes for model selection or parameter tuning.
Retain negative, null, and failed evidence rather than revising the report.
notes: MAE = mean absolute error; RMSE = root mean squared error; sMAPE = mean(200|ŷ-y|/(|y|+|ŷ|)).

robustness_tests: Replacing saturated row-40 feature value with the training median reduced ridge locked-test MAE from 1.885911 to 1.305282, RMSE to 1.745295, and sMAPE to 1.466762%.
Excluding saturated row 40 from ridge scoring yielded MAE 0.950240, RMSE 1.064821, and sMAPE 1.064734% on n=9.
Injecting missing feature values at predefined test rows 41 and 46 and imputing them with the training median worsened ridge MAE to 2.510330, RMSE to 3.837316, and sMAPE to 2.912610%.
A paired bootstrap with seed 20260901 and 2000 replicates quantified uncertainty in the ridge-minus-persistence test MAE difference.
Two complete executions produced byte-identical output, verifying deterministic randomness control.
selected_model: Ridge regression with penalty 1.0 using intercept, feature, and lag1, selected using validation folds only; its claimed superiority was subsequently falsified on the locked test set.

The paired-bootstrap interval crosses zero; it does not establish a reliable population-level difference between ridge and persistence.

Target and feature units, operational loss asymmetry, forecast horizon terminology, and deployment latency are unspecified.
The selected ridge uses unscaled predictors and a fixed penalty; broader hyperparameter search was intentionally avoided to prevent test-driven tuning.
Synthetic invalid date labels prevent calendar-frequency or seasonality claims.
